presets.name: Sleep
presets.wording: Often used to wind down before sleep.

sources.title: A Novel Insight of Effects of a 3-Hz Binaural Beat on Sleep Stages During Sleep
sources.finding: 24 people, one night. A 3 Hz beat was played during sleep. The group that heard it spent longer in deep sleep (stage N3) and reached it sooner than the group that heard silence.

sources.title: Minimal Effects of Binaural Auditory Beats for Subclinical Insomnia: A Randomized Double-Blind Controlled Study
sources.finding: 43 people with mild insomnia. Music with a theta beat for 30 minutes before bed, for 2 weeks, did not improve sleep more than the same music without the beat.

presets.evidenceNote: No study we found tested a 2 Hz beat before sleep. These are the closest.

presets.name: Calm
presets.wording: Often used for meditation and relaxation.

sources.title: Brain Responses to a 6-Hz Binaural Beat: Effects on General Theta Rhythm and Frontal Midline Theta Activity
sources.finding: 28 people. A 6 Hz beat for 30 minutes. Theta activity in the brain rose within 10 minutes, and people reported less tension than the control group.

sources.title: A prospective, randomised, controlled study examining binaural beat audio and pre-operative anxiety in patients undergoing general anaesthesia for day case surgery
sources.finding: Patients waiting for day surgery. Anxiety scores fell 26.3% with binaural beat audio, 11.1% with the same audio without beats, and 3.8% with no audio.

sources.authors: Fatima, Zaidi, Sundus, Alam, Parveen and Khan
sources.title: Efficacy of theta binaural beat therapy on pain, cognition and anxiety in adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
sources.finding: A review of 13 randomized trials (630 people) of theta beats, 4 to 8 Hz. Anxiety fell mainly in people facing a medical procedure or living with chronic pain. The anxiety results were too different to combine into one number.

presets.name: Relaxed focus
presets.wording: Often used for calm, steady attention.

sources.authors: Rakhshan, Hassani-Abharian, Joghataei, Nasehi and Khosrowabadi
sources.title: Effects of the Alpha, Beta, and Gamma Binaural Beat Brain Stimulation and Short-Term Training on Simultaneously Assessed Visuospatial and Verbal Working Memories
sources.finding: 31 people, 8 minutes per sound. A 10 Hz beat gave a few small gains on a visual memory task and worse results on a listening task.

sources.authors: Beauchene, Abaid, Moran, Diana and Leonessa
sources.title: The Effect of Binaural Beats on Visuospatial Working Memory and Cortical Connectivity
sources.finding: A 10 Hz beat during a visual memory task lowered accuracy. A 15 Hz beat raised it.

sources.title: Potential of binaural beats intervention for improving memory and attention: insights from meta-analysis and systematic review
sources.finding: A meta-analysis of 15 studies found a medium effect on memory and attention overall (g = 0.40), with conflicting results between studies.

presets.name: Focus
presets.wording: Often used for active work and concentration.

sources.title: Binaural auditory beats affect vigilance performance and mood
sources.finding: 29 people, a 30 minute watch-keeping task. With 16 and 24 Hz beats they caught more targets and made fewer false alarms than with 1.5 and 4 Hz beats.

sources.authors: Robison, Obulasetty, Blais, Wingert and Brewer
sources.title: The effect of binaural beat stimulation on sustained attention
sources.finding: Three experiments with a 16 Hz beat. Taken together, the authors found rather strong evidence against a benefit for sustained attention.

sources.authors: Beauchene, Abaid, Moran, Diana and Leonessa
sources.title: The Effect of Binaural Beats on Visuospatial Working Memory and Cortical Connectivity
sources.finding: A 15 Hz beat during a visual memory task raised accuracy. 5 Hz and 10 Hz beats lowered it.

presets.evidenceNote: No study we found tested 18 Hz exactly. These used 15, 16 and 24 Hz.

sources.authors: Engelbregt, Barmentlo, Keeser, Pogarell and Deijen
sources.title: Effects of binaural and monaural beat stimulation on attention and EEG
sources.finding: 25 students. Fewer errors on an attention task with a 40 Hz beat than with pink noise. Brain recordings did not show the brain matching the beat.

sources.authors: Engelbregt, Meijburg, Schulten, Pogarell and Deijen
sources.title: The Effects of Binaural and Monoaural Beat Stimulation on Cognitive Functioning in Subjects with Different Levels of Emotionality
sources.finding: 24 people. Faster on an attention task with a 40 Hz beat than with white noise, but a plain 40 Hz pulse in both ears did the same. No change in working memory.

sources.title: Influence of Binaural Beats Stimulation of Gamma Frequency over Memory Performance and EEG Spectral Density
sources.finding: 30 people. A 40 Hz beat made no difference to memory task results or to brain recordings.
